interpretation: The history effect is directionally stronger when another seagrass remains in the loss year, but the frozen interaction interval overlaps zero. The data therefore do not support a robust history-by-community-continuity synergy; the bare-state null may reflect limited sample size or broader site-state differences.
next_hypothesis: Decompose pre-loss history into focal Thalassia run length versus generic any-seagrass habitat headstart to test whether the supported pooled history signal is focal-specific or a marker of persistent vegetated microsites.
claim_boundary: Post-hoc interaction test on an already-opened recovery endpoint.
Do not claim a formally supported synergy between local history and alternative-seagrass continuity.
The positive vegetated-only coefficient and higher return fraction are descriptive secondary patterns, not substitutes for the failed interaction support rule.
Do not infer facilitation, rhizome memory, or causal community effects.
Return is recorded reappearance, not genet-level recolonization.
